findings.situation: A filer whose employer paid tips in two jobs, one on the tipped-occupation list (such as server) and one not on it, gets a Form W-2 box 7 that covers both, and the question tells them the amount is 'taken from one of these', including box 7.
findings.source_text: i1040gi p. 103: 'If you received tips as an employee in more than one occupation for the same employer, only those tips that were received in an occupation on the list of occupations that customarily and regularly received tips on or before December 31, 2024, are considered qualified tips. Do not include tips received in occupations that are not included on this list in line 4a, 4b, or 4c.'
findings.why: The question says 'Qualified tips from this employer, taken from one of these (your choice): Form W-2 box 7...', and neither it nor its help explains the occupation limit. One filer will copy the box 7 total, while another will enter only the listed-occupation share, so the two give different column (b) amounts.

locators: p. 103, "If you received tips as an employee in more than one occupation for the same employer, only those tips that were received in an occupation on the list ... are considered qualified tips. Do not include tips received in occupations that are not included on this list in line 4a, 4b, or 4c"

findings.situation: A gambling dealer (TTOC 201) receives tips in casino chips or other tokens that can be exchanged for a fixed amount, and truthfully answers no because chips are not 'cash, check, card or app'.
findings.source_text: i1040gi p. 102: "paid in a cash medium, including by cash, check, credit card, debit card, gift card, tangible or intangible tokens that are readily exchangeable for a fixed amount (for example, casino chips), and any other form of electronic settlement or mobile payment app"
findings.why: The question defines cash only as 'cash (including by check, card or app)'. It leaves out tokens such as casino chips, which the text counts as a cash medium. A filer whose tips are all qualified may therefore answer no, and tipjob.mixed is set to true when it should be false.

locators: p. 103, Schedule 1-A, "Determining the amount of qualified tips received by an employee for 2025"
